sources.citation: P. C. Wason (1968). Reasoning about a Rule. Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1968) in Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Peter C. Wason (1969). Regression in Reasoning? British Journal of Psychology.
sources.notes: Documents persistent self-justifying rationalization when participants confront hypothetical contradictions on the abstract four-card task.

sources.citation: P. N. Johnson-Laird, Paolo Legrenzi, Maria Sonino Legrenzi (1972). Reasoning and a Sense of Reality. British Journal of Psychology.
sources.notes: Demonstrates dramatic facilitation on realistic postal-stamp rule-checking versions of the Wason selection task.

sources.citation: Jonathan St. B. T. Evans (1984). Heuristic and analytic processes in reasoning. British Journal of Psychology.
sources.notes: Demonstrates surface perceptual 'matching bias' toward cards named in the rule independent of logical negation.

sources.citation: Richard A. Griggs, James R. Cox (1982). The elusive thematic‐materials effect in Wason's selection task. British Journal of Psychology.
sources.notes: Griggs & Cox's 1982 drinking-age thematic replication proving real-world rule familiarity unlocks modus tollens falsification.

sources.citation: Eric-Jan Wagenmakers (2009). How do individuals reason in the Wason card selection task? Behavioral and Brain Sciences.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2009) in How do individuals reason in the Wason card selection task? Behavioral and Brain Sciences extending the foundational findings.
